tasks.short: Supervise overt detection and criminal processing of theft cases

steps.what: Supervise the surveillance case queue
Assign an owner for criminal processing
Handle in-person detection of theft
Record the criminal processing checklist
Decide the next processing step
File the signed processing status

tasks.design: Overt alarm events a loss prevention officer has already logged sit on a {WORKFLOW} queue with store, device, time, owner and due date. The loss prevention manager assigns an owner and decides the next criminal-processing step, then that signed status is filed in {DOCS}. Floor detection stays in person. The queue does not score staff and does not add a camera.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case age and owner lived in call notes, so a case could sit with no next step and nobody could see the gap from a list.
tasks.enabler_now: An event the officer already logged can carry a case id, a device id and a due date, which is enough to show age and owner.
tasks.still_hard: What should happen next on a criminal case, and what a person on the floor saw, still depend on people.
tasks.human_edge: The manager chooses the owner and the next processing step, and can leave a case untouched.

ambition.what: Check every open processing case for an owner and a due date each week, not only when a store calls

tasks.altitude: The queue shows which cases have no owner. The manager does not gain a new way to watch staff, and floor detection stays with the officer.

reach.task: Log the overt detection event and carry out the processing step the manager named
reach.learn: Which cases have an owner and which next step was signed

evidence.claim: Digest [S12] says works council consent is needed before staff monitoring, so this queue uses logged alarm events and does not open a new watch on staff.
Digest [S9] says GDPR article 22 does not allow a solely automated decision about a person, so the next step on a case is the manager's decision.
Digest [S3] says incident reports are forwarded to the person in charge, which matches a queue the manager supervises rather than a case that moves itself.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task is supervision of detection and criminal processing already under way. It does not add cameras, hidden or overt, and it does not score staff.

Input contract: case id, store id, device id, event time, disposition code, owner, due date. Producer is the loss prevention officer for the event, and the manager for owner and due date. Events with no case id stay off the queue. No employee id and no video review are inputs.

If works council consent for staff monitoring is absent, the queue is limited to alarm counts and case age, not footage of staff. Native workflow lists are configured before custom code. Interviews stay in person with the officer.
unknowns: Whether current alarm logs include footage or only a device event.
Who may be named as case owner.
Whether consent for any staff-facing camera is already on file.
research_questions: What share of open cases have no owner or no due date?
How many logged events are alarm counts rather than a person stopped in the store?

already_counted.description: Manager time choosing a case owner stays in that decision
Manager time on the next processing step stays in that decision

incremental.description: Keep the queue fields aligned with the alarm events the stores actually log
Officers correct an event that arrived with no case id

approvals.approved_version: case owner signed for this case id
processing decision signed in this review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes events are still free-text calls, so the queue stays thin and supervision remains a meeting. The high case assumes a clean event list but every owner choice, the floor detection and the next processing step stay with a person. No new surveillance is counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Audit store cash and investigate deposit gaps

steps.what: Sign the cash match fields for the week
Export till totals and deposit amounts
Match declared cash to the deposit
Explain a gap the match cannot close
Perform deposit investigations on the gaps
Sign the store cash audit result
File the signed cash audit

tasks.design: The loss prevention manager signs the match fields for the week: store, date, till total, declared cash and deposit amount, with no employee id. A {BI} check against the {ERP} and the {BANK} marks gaps only. The cash office explains a gap, the manager investigates, and only a signed cash result is filed. Any action about a named person is a separate human decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Till totals, declared cash and deposit slips sat in different extracts, so a gap was found by rekeying rather than by a shared store-day.
tasks.enabler_now: Till, declared cash and the bank deposit can share a store id and a business date.
tasks.still_hard: A gap the totals cannot explain still needs someone who was there, and blaming a person is not a calculation.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides whether a gap is explained, needs a recount, or must be referred to a person.

ambition.what: Sign a cash result for every store week that has a gap, not only when finance asks

tasks.altitude: Clean store-days drop off the list. The manager's week is the unexplained gaps, and no rule names an employee.

reach.task: Explain a deposit gap the match could not close
reach.learn: Which store-days matched and which gaps the manager has already signed

evidence.claim: In a mid-size retailer a cash audit is a match of till totals, declared cash and the bank deposit, and the hard part is the gap those totals do not explain.
Digest [S2] describes GRC modules for compliance, audit, incident and regulatory monitoring, which can hold an audit result a person signs.
Digest [S9] says GDPR article 22 does not allow a solely automated decision about a person, so a cash gap is not an action about an employee.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task ends at a signed cash result or a referral. A referral about a named employee is the manager's decision and is not produced by the match.

Input contract: store id, business date, tender, till total, declared cash, deposit amount, bank reference. Producer is the cash office export and the bank statement. No employee id. A row with no store id, no date or no deposit amount stays on a manual list.

Native exports from the till record and the bank feed are configured before custom code. The meeting prior overstates this task: most time is on the totals, and only unexplained gaps become a conversation.
unknowns: Whether every store deposits daily or in batches.
Who may sign a result when the manager is absent.
Whether finance or the loss prevention manager owns the first recount.
research_questions: What share of store-days lack a bank reference?
How many gaps are explained by a timing difference rather than missing cash?

already_counted.description: Manager time on unexplained gaps stays in the investigation
Manager time signing the cash result stays in that decision

incremental.description: Revise match fields when a new tender or deposit pattern appears
Cash office resubmits a deposit row missing a bank reference

approvals.approved_version: cash match fields signed for this week
the same signed cash match fields
cash audit result signed for this store week
the same signed cash audit result

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many deposits lack a bank reference, so the match rarely runs and the manager still ties out by hand. The high case assumes clean totals but every unexplained gap and every signed result stay with the manager. Time spent speaking to a named employee is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend changes to programs, staffing, scheduling or training

steps.what: Gather shrink, audit and training figures
Draft improvements on staffing, scheduling and training

loop.input: store period figures and the note template
loop.output: note that cites store and period only
loop.check: Every figure equals the extract and no sentence names or ranks a person
loop.stop: One draft; drop any sentence with no store id
loop.why_not_simpler: Whether a store needs hours or training is not a lookup on the extract

steps.what: Comment on staffing and training ideas
Recommend changes to the prevention programs
File the signed recommendation

tasks.design: Shrink units, open audit fails, training completions and vacant hours land on a {BI} view by store, with no behaviour score. A bounded note in {DOCS} may cite only those figures. The loss prevention manager decides which recommendations to send. The note does not build a roster, and any change to a named person's hours stays a later human decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: The figures behind a recommendation were collected ad hoc, so a draft could not show which store and period it used.
tasks.enabler_now: Shrink, audit fails and training completions can be exported by store and period.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a store needs people, hours or a different procedure is still a management judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The manager chooses which recommendations go forward and which figures are not enough.

ambition.what: Put a recommendation forward every quarter from the signed figures, not only after a crisis

tasks.altitude: Less time hunting figures, the same decision on what to recommend. The manager can block a sentence that does not cite a store and a period.

reach.task: Respond to the signed recommendation on staffing or training
reach.learn: Which stores the manager included and which ideas were dropped

evidence.claim: Digest [S15] says a model-drafted paid report cited sources that did not exist, so a person stays on a recommendation before it is sent.
Digest [S9] says GDPR article 22 does not allow a solely automated decision about a person, so the note does not change anyone's hours or post.
Digest [S12] says works council consent is needed before staff monitoring, and this recommendation uses store totals rather than a watch on staff.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task ends at a signed recommendation. Building a roster or changing a named person's hours is out of scope and is not counted as saved.

Input contract: store id, period, shrink units, open audit fails, training completions, vacant loss-prevention hours. Producer is the store totals export. No employee id and no behaviour score. A store with no period is left out of the draft.
Native dashboard tiles are configured before custom code. Scheduling in this task means a sentence about hours short, not a shift plan.
unknowns: Who receives the recommendation besides retail operations.
Whether vacant hours are stored as a number or only as a comment.
Whether training completions are in a learning record the manager may read.
research_questions: What share of stores have shrink, audit fails and training completions for the same period?
How often is a recommendation sent back because a figure was wrong?

already_counted.description: Manager edits a sentence that does not match the figures
Manager time choosing what to recommend stays in that decision

incremental.description: Revise the figure set when a new training record or shrink definition appears
Operations managers send back a store whose figures look wrong

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the figures stay in separate notes, so the draft rarely cites a clean store-period and the manager still assembles them. The high case assumes clean figures but every recommendation is still signed by the manager. Roster building is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct an overt camera install and refuse a covert one

steps.what: Write the request for security cameras
Refuse covert surveillance of staff
Survey the site for an overt camera
Direct the overt installation or stop
Release the signed install work order
Install only the signed overt camera

tasks.design: The loss prevention manager records place, purpose and whether staff can be seen on a {WORKFLOW} form. A covert purpose, or a view of staff with no works-council consent, stops there and produces no install method. Only a signed overt version becomes a {DOCS} work order, and the installer does the physical work in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Camera requests were conversations, so there was no signed purpose that could stop a hidden watch before an installer was called.
tasks.enabler_now: A request can store place, purpose and a consent reference as fields, which is enough to refuse a covert purpose by rule.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a purpose is acceptable, and whether staff are in view, is still the manager's judgement, and the installer still visits the site.
tasks.human_edge: The manager refuses hidden watching and signs or stops an overt install.
tasks.altitude: The manager can stop a covert request before anyone is called. Directing a rare install stays an in-person decision, and no hidden camera is designed.

reach.task: Install only the overt camera named on the signed work order
reach.learn: Which requests were refused and which overt places were signed

evidence.claim: Digest [S12] says works council consent is needed before staff monitoring, including loss-prevention monitoring of staff.
Digest [S9] says GDPR article 22 does not allow a solely automated decision about a person, so a request to watch a named person is refused rather than processed.
Directing a camera install in a mid-size retailer is rare and done in person. A form can record the purpose. It cannot decide the purpose.

assumptions: Focal role is the loss prevention manager. The task ends at a refused request or a signed overt work order. Covert placement, concealment and any method of hidden watching are out of scope and are not designed.

Input contract: site id, place description, purpose code (entrance, stock room, cash office, other), whether staff can be seen, consent reference or blank, covert flag. Producer is the loss prevention manager. If the covert flag is true, the purpose is to watch a named person, or staff can be seen and the consent reference is blank, the only output is a refusal.
Native request forms are configured before custom code. The in-person prior is right: survey and install stay on site. A refusal releases no work order.
unknowns: Whether a works council consent for overt cameras is already on file.
Who may sign when the manager is absent.
Which sites already have an overt camera the request would duplicate.
research_questions: How many camera requests in a year are covert or name a person to watch?
How many overt installs wait because the consent reference is blank?

already_counted.description: Manager time refusing a covert purpose stays in that decision
Manager time directing the install stays on site

incremental.description: Keep the purpose codes and the consent check aligned with the current consent record

approvals.approved_version: purpose decision signed for this request
overt install decision signed on site
the same signed overt install decision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes almost every request is refused or handled entirely in person, so only the form is new. The high case assumes an overt request with consent on file, while the refusal, the site survey and the install stay with people. No covert install is treated as saved or as built.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Cash gaps and overt case queues are reviewed as lists, recommendations become a signed note, and a covert camera request stops instead of becoming a way to watch staff.
reach: The cash office clerk receives the signed cash audit instead of a mailbox thread.
A security manager sees which camera requests were refused and which overt work orders were released.
skills_to_grow: Separate a till-total gap from any action about a named person.
Write a recommendation that cites figures and does not set a roster.
Stop a camera request whose purpose is hidden watching of staff.
role.ambitious_version: Every store week with a cash gap has a signed result, and no camera is installed without a signed overt purpose.
